_doc: FLEET-MAP-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25: "what really needs to be in the ultra-stable template repo as opposed to these other repos that you created ... it's starting to look like a mess ... create your own instructions and fail-safe ways to make sure it all works together every single time it's deployed for every tenant, any code agent, everything."). One row per repository of the org: what it is for, its layer, what it is copied from (source path, the workflow that copies it, direction), which Workers deploy from it, whether it runs Actions, where it runs (live, equal to what fleetcontract reads from the registries), its visibility and the instruction file an agent reads there. Read by foundation/fleetmap.py: --check (in checks) fails when a repository named in doctrine/tenant-repos.json, doctrine/full-stack.json (seeds of doctrine/seed-deploys.json), github/org-settings.json or session_repos below has no row, when a row is in none of them, and when a synced_from names a path or workflow that does not exist; --drift compares every mirror with its source (a clone beside this checkout, or the public GitHub tree) and reports differ, missing, extra or unmeasured, never ok without a reading; --drift --apply files Q-FLEETMAP-<repo> per mirror that is not equal and closes it when the same reading passes. Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system. SYSTEM-MANIFEST-1: the purpose, layer, live address, visibility and deploys of a row are not typed here; `fleetmap --gen` reads them from the ultrastable.json manifest at the root of each repository (seed/standards/system.schema.json), and --check fails a live or planned repository whose manifest was not found. What a row adds by hand is only what a manifest cannot know about itself: what it is copied from, by which workflow, and the instruction file.

layers.platform: the one repository where code and rules are written; everything else is copied from it or vendors from it
layers.template: a published copy of the platform's seed/ folder, the kernel a new system starts from; never edited by hand
layers.seeded-system: a system started from the kernel; owns its idea, instance and domain content, receives the kernel by sync
layers.tenant: an app the platform runs; owns its app code, vendors named core files
layers.admin: the company's own papers and ledgers; not code
layers.org-profile: the organization's public profile and community defaults

template_contents._doc: TEMPLATE-CODE-ONLY-1: what belongs in ultrastable/seed. It is seed/ of the platform, plus the files in keep. Anything else there is drift: either kernel code to move up into seed/ or a file to delete. generated: files a generator in seed/ writes from the tree; the template's copy is output, never work to carry up, so a publish replaces it. retired: files the template still holds that seed/ carries under another name; a publish removes them (Q-FLEETMAP-seed).

generated.reason: Written by scripts/system.py --write from autonomy/system.json and the code of record; the file itself says not to edit it by hand. The template's copy listed doctrine/balance.json only because the retired duplicate was still there.

retired.reason: The same rules, key for key, as autonomy/balance.json, which has the schema (autonomy/schemas/balance.schema.json). scripts/balance.py reads doctrine/ first, so the duplicate shadowed the config of record.
The first form of the system definition (SYSTEM-1); scripts/system.py reads autonomy/system.json and has no --gen, which this file's own text calls.
stepPlan and its step lists are defined and exported by tick.js, which never imported this copy; nothing in the kit imports it.
Tests the unused copy; tick.test.js tests the stepPlan the tick runs.

session_repos._doc: Repositories a cloud session of 2026-11-25 had cloned beside the platform; a repository that exists and is in no registry is caught here.

ultrastable/ultrastable.purpose: The platform: all code, rules, doctrine, the website, the dashboard and the seed/ kernel are written here and nowhere else.

ultrastable/seed.purpose: The code-only kernel a new autonomous system starts from: bootstrapper, tick Worker, roles, agent instructions and the loops that take it to criticality. A copy of seed/ in the Ultrastable platform.

ultrastable/second-tenant.purpose: The first system started from the kernel with no code agent: proof that seed/ alone boots, deploys and runs a system.

ultrastable/ops.purpose: The company's own admin, legal and business papers, backups and sealed audit ledgers; no code deploys from it.
ultrastable/ops.visibility_reason: company admin, legal and backup ledgers (TEMPLATE-CODE-ONLY-1); the one marked exception to DISCOVER-1

ultrastable/.github.purpose: The organization's public profile page and community health defaults.
ultrastable/.github.visibility_reason: GitHub shows an org profile only from a public .github repository

ultrastable/practical-solutions.purpose: Tenant app Practical Solutions (ultrastable.org): evidence-based solutions to global problems.
ultrastable/practical-solutions.deploys_by: its own repository's pipeline (deploy-tenant.yml), not the platform's deploy lane

ultrastable/unlearn.purpose: Unlearn: popular beliefs where the evidence points another way, with graded evidence, named sources and a loop that keeps checking them.

ultrastable/what-works.purpose: What Works: a living atlas of what works in public policy, every programme graded by its trials and re-graded as evidence lands.

ultrastable/replication-ledger.purpose: Replication Ledger: which landmark findings held up and which failed, across many fields, updated as replications publish.

ultrastable/base-rates.purpose: Before you decide, see what usually happens: graded base rates for life, work and policy choices, and your own forecasting record.

ultrastable/did-it-work.purpose: Every big policy promised something. See what it promised, what the evaluations found since, and how the verdict moved.

ultrastable/open-questions.purpose: What science honestly does not know yet: the big open questions, where the evidence leans today, and how that lean has moved.

ultrastable/workers.purpose: Retired: the core Worker code moved into the platform under workers/.
ultrastable/workers.visibility_reason: kept public so existing links resolve

redundant.evidence: github/org-settings.json describes it as retired; the code is workers/ in the platform

ultrastable/spec.purpose: Retired: the specifications moved into the platform (specs/, SCOPE.md, licensing/).
ultrastable/spec.visibility_reason: kept public so existing links resolve

ultrastable/license.purpose: Retired: the licence text moved into the platform (LICENSE, licensing/).
ultrastable/license.visibility_reason: kept public so existing links resolve

ultrastable/spinoffs.purpose: Retired: the eight generated apps that shared one Worker; replaced by one repository per tenant.
ultrastable/spinoffs.visibility_reason: kept public so existing links resolve

identity._doc: LIVE-LINKS-1: what a seeded system owns and no sync may overwrite. The kernel sync (foundation/upstream.py OWNED) leaves these alone; the step that fills a new repository from seed/ renders README.md for the system (its own title and Live block) instead of copying the template's.
